title: Applications of Communication in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Competitive Robotics
members: Andrew Needham, Charles Malohn, Corbin Shaffer, Jacob Newberry, Leigh Goetsch
description: An overview of how attention-based communication allows autonomous teams of robots to coordinate efficiently in dynamic settings while using limited bandwidth.
content:
## Abstract

Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a robust framework for complex robotic behaviors,
yet communication constraints like bandwidth limitations and latency remain a challenge
in dynamic environments. This paper presents a multi-agent RL environment designed
for the VEX Artificial Intelligence Robotics Competition (VAIRC). We trained agents
using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with a multi-headed architecture including a
primary action head and an attention-based communication head for latent messaging. The
system integrates real-time object detection and nonlinear trajectory optimization to bridge
the gap between simulation and physical deployment. Results indicate that RL-driven
approaches generate effective strategies for the VAIRC environment. Crucially, our findings
demonstrate that communication between agents improves scoring efficiency compared to
independent agent models, and that attention-based communication remains resilient to loss
of information, proving the viability of coordinated RL in high-stakes robotics.
